page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The hardware includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications consist of 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2688.09, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21511.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7817.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, measuring 95.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 51.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Cryptographic and compression tasks also perform within the average tier, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 8969.12 and single-threaded gzip compression at 25.93 GB/sec.

The instance offers a balanced resource profile, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or compute-optimized hardware. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility for high-speed database logging or intensive machine learning training. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, as reflected by its static web serving throughput of 11.61 GB/sec and Passmark database score of 6859.59.
